summary.headline: Priced far above its own history and peers, while profit shrinks
summary.takeaway: Investors pay much more than usual for each dollar of Tesla's profit and sales, and far more than similar companies. Profit fell over the past year, so recent growth does not explain the high price.

positives.text: Sales were about flat over the past year (-0.2%), better than the peer median of -2%.
Wall Street analysts estimate EPS (profit per share) will grow 25.2% next year, giving a lower forward P/E of 178.

watch_outs.text: P/E (price compared with yearly profit) is 424, higher than 94% of the last 5 years and far above the peer median of 22.5.
EPS fell 43.6% over the past year and 33.2% per year over 3 years, so growth does not explain the price.
DCF estimates (value from future cash, based on assumptions) range $28.20 to $37.02 per share, far below the $384.68 price.
